I have cleaned teeth for fifteen years, and there is one question I ask every patient: how often do you floss? Almost everybody says every day. About one in ten actually does. I know, because the gums always tell the truth. So these days I ask the question differently. I say: when did you last floss? That question gets an honest answer, because it asks about one day, not about a habit. And the honest answer is usually useful. Most people floss two or three times a week, normally in the evening, and hardly ever in the morning, because mornings are a rush. My advice is not to promise every day. Floss once a day, at the same time, right after something you never skip, like brushing your teeth at night. A small habit attached to a big one almost always survives. A small habit on its own almost never does.

We have two kids and two jobs, so our week only works because it repeats. On Mondays and Wednesdays my son has soccer after school, so I leave the office early on those days. My daughter has piano once a week, on Thursdays, and my wife takes her. Every other Friday we have pizza night, and the kids choose the movie, which means we usually watch the same three movies. Once a month we drive to my parents' house for Sunday lunch. That is the normal schedule. Do we stick to it? Most weeks, yes. Now and then something breaks. A meeting runs late, or somebody forgets the soccer bag at home, and then we change one thing, not everything. The rule in our house is simple: we can move a day, but we never cancel pizza night.
